name: Steve Albini
hook: A recording engineer who refused to be called a producer, refused royalties, and recorded the Pixies and Nirvana to sound like a band in a room.

blurb.age13: Steve Albini was born in 1962 and led the Chicago band Big Black in the 1980s, which used a drum machine instead of a drummer. He became famous for recording other bands. He called himself a recording engineer, not a producer, charged a flat fee, and refused royalties. He recorded the Pixies' 'Surfer Rosa' in 1988 and Nirvana's 'In Utero' in 1993. He died in 2024.
blurb.adult: Born in Pasadena in 1962; he formed Big Black at Northwestern University in 1981, with a Roland TR-606 drum machine in place of a drummer, and they split in 1987. As an engineer he rejected the producer title and producer royalties, turning down about $500,000 in royalties on 'In Utero' for a flat $100,000 fee; his day rate at his death was $900. His method was to capture the sound of the room with careful microphone placement. He founded Electrical Audio in Chicago in 1995 and died in 2024. Big Black's use of the TR-606 is the first documented TR-606 record this map has found (see BACKLOG's held machines).
